artworks.title: Slaughter of the Suitors (with Philoetius)
artworks.description: Campanian red-figure bell-krater in the Louvre (CA 7124): Odysseus and Telemachus cut down the suitors with Eumaeus and Philoetius at their side — the cowherd who locked the doors and killed Peisander. Homer's loyal stockman leaves the herds for the hall's climax.

films.title: The Odyssey
films.description: Konchalovsky's miniseries keeps the loyal cowherd among the few who stand with Odysseus — Philoetius beside Eumaeus at the return.

films.title: L'Odissea
films.description: Rossi's Odyssey stages the Ithacan servants who never betrayed the king — Philoetius as the cowherd of the slaughter.

popCulture.title: Odyssey
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Books 20–22 make Philoetius Odysseus' chief cowherd — loyal through twenty years, locksmith of the hall, and killer of the suitor Peisander.

popCulture.title: Philoetius
popCulture.description: The Odyssey's cowherd counterpart to Eumaeus — promised freedom and power for remaining faithful when other slaves turned.
